To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the phosphoric acid sorption in Nafion 117 is characterized by the formation of hydrogen bonding interactions, 2) the sorbed phosphoric acid is in the same chemical environment as the bulk phosphoric acid, and 3) the phosphoric-acid-sorbed membrane is in a state of equilibrium between the sulfonic-acid groups, residual water and sorbed phosphoric-acid molecules.
1H and31P NMR measurements of the H3PO4-sorbed Nafion® membrane indicate a high mobility and a strong exchange of protons with the sulfonic groups.

the 31P NMF signal for phosphoric acids sorbed in Nfion is broadened compared to the signal in 100% phosphorics acid in bulk liquid, and that in the 1H NMR spectrum for HPO4-equilibratied Nfion, the peak is shifted downfield compared with the peak of a relatively dry membrane, and is relatively broad.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of NMR spectroscopy to examine proton transport in Nafion membranes equilibrated with various concentrations of H3PO 4.
the characterization of the structure of Nafion® membrane equilibrated with phosphoric acid using 1H NMR and 31P MAS NMR spectroscopic techniques.
the characterization of H3PO 4-equilibrated and water-equilibrated Nafion 117 membranes by 1H and31P NMR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phosphoric acid is sorbed as a proton donor in Nafion membranes, but the exact structure of the sorbed species and the mechanism of proton exchange between −SO−3H and HPO4−3 is yet to be determined.
the 1H and especially the 31P NMF spectroscopy can be used to characterize H3PO4 in the Nafion membrane.

the phosphoric acid sorption into the Nafion® membrane is a complex process that involves the formation of hydrogen-bonding interactions, exchange of acidic protons between phosphoric acid, sulfonic acid and water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phosphoric acid in H3PO4 equilibrated Nafions is not strongly immobilized in the membrane, and is not in the same environment as in the bulk acid.
the phosphoric acid in Nafion is not in the form of H3PO3, H3PO4 or any other acid, but rather a mixture of these species, with the exact mixture depending on the relative humidity and temperature.

H3PO4 equilibration results in an increase in −SO3H acidity, and a reduction in the number of available protons in the −SO3H groups, which may be due to the formation of hydrogen bonds between −SO3− and −PO3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
1H and, in particular, 31P NMF spectroscopy are useful for probing the state of H3PO3 in Nafion membranes.
the NMR spectroscopy is a very powerful tool in the analysis of the proton transport in Nafion membranes.
the phosphoric acid is sorbed in Nfion® 117 membrane in a form that is not significantly different from that in bulk phosphoric acid.
